title: eval-harness: integrate prompt-regression metrics into CI checks and add quality gating hook
author: Asha Patel
description: Context: We need deterministic CI-level regression detection for prompt-set quality to avoid user-facing regressions after model or prompt changes. This PR wires eval-harness metrics into the GitHub CI pipeline and adds a quality-gating hook that fails the PR when configured thresholds are exceeded. What this does: 1) Adds a new CI job (eval-regression-check) that runs a lightweight subset of eval-harness prompt sets on the diff and computes delta metrics (accuracy/rouge/emt/embedding-sim). 2) Integrates metric thresholds from linear tickets (ENG-7421) and allows per-repo/per-branch overrides via .eval/config.yaml. 3) Adds a gating hook that posts a structured check with top-level summary, per-prompt regressions, and links to the full evaluation artifact in S3. 4) Adds unit/integration tests and developer docs for enabling/disabling gating and for tuning thresholds. Motivation: CI-level gating prevents accidental degradations from model upgrades and prompt refactors; it provides actionable signals to authors (top failing prompts, suggested rollback candidates). Backwards compatibility: gating is opt-in by default; repos with existing workflows can adopt incrementally. Checklist: - [x] Add CI job and workflow YAML - [x] Hook eval-harness to produce standardized JSON metrics - [x] Add gating logic and config parsing - [x] Add tests and fixtures - [x] Docs/Devguide updated - [x] Smoke-tested on a small internal repo Link to proposal: docs/internal/eval-harness/ci-gating-proposal.md Related: ENG-7480 (quality gating runtime), SUP-3321 (customer incident prompting this change).
